storm.title: SUPER TYPHOON
storm.name: CHAMPI
storm.names: Philippines: Rosal · Taiwan: 薔琵 · Japan: 台風30号 チャンパー

show_open.label: Show open
show_open.content: A short cold open introducing a continuously updating watch on Super Typhoon Champi (薔琵) as it approaches Taiwan. Sets expectations that the information refreshes throughout the stream.

storm_position.label: Current storm position
storm_position.content: The current position of Super Typhoon Champi (Taiwan name 薔琵, JTWC 29W, JMA typhoon 2630) relative to Taiwan: distance and direction from Taiwan's east coast, intensity (sustained winds, gusts, central pressure) and movement, as reported by Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA), JMA and JTWC, with the time of each analysis.

track_forecast.label: Track and intensity forecast
track_forecast.content: The forecast track and intensity of Super Typhoon Champi (薔琵) over the next 72 to 120 hours as it relates to Taiwan: when CWA expects to issue sea and land typhoon warnings, the closest approach to Taiwan, the expected northward turn, the chance of landfall on the east coast, forecast uncertainty, and any disagreement between CWA, JMA and JTWC.

local_impacts.label: Expected local impacts in Taiwan
local_impacts.content: Expected impacts of Super Typhoon Champi (薔琵) in Taiwan, especially Yilan, Hualien, Taitung, Taipei, New Taipei and Keelung and the central mountains: CWA sea and land typhoon warnings, heavy and torrential rain advisories and rainfall totals, strong-wind probabilities, rough seas, ferry and flight disruptions, and any work and school closures announced by city and county governments, each attributed to the issuing authority.

show_close.label: Show close
show_close.content: A brief sign-off reminding viewers in Taiwan that the broadcast loops with refreshed data on Typhoon Champi (薔琵) and pointing them to the Central Weather Administration and their city or county government for warnings and closure decisions.

anchor_neutral.label: Neutral news anchor
anchor_neutral.content: You are writing copy to be read aloud by a single news anchor. Write in plain spoken English for viewers in Taiwan. Write in complete sentences, with no headings, bullet points, stage directions, or markdown. Lead with the most recent and most decision-relevant fact. Attribute every claim to its source agency by name. Never invent numbers, timestamps, or place names that are not present in the supplied source material; if a figure is missing, say that it has not been reported. Target roughly 220 to 260 seconds (about 4 minutes) of spoken delivery. Use the time to cover every reported detail and explain how the pieces fit together, not to repeat yourself.

anchor_urgent.label: Urgent safety bulletin
anchor_urgent.content: You are writing an urgent public-safety bulletin to be read aloud by a single anchor. Write in plain spoken English for viewers in Taiwan. Use short, direct sentences. Lead with the specific action the audience should take and the areas affected. Attribute every instruction to the issuing authority. Never invent an evacuation order, a shelter location, a suspension or a casualty figure that is not present in the supplied source material. Do not speculate beyond what the sources state. Target roughly 220 to 260 seconds (about 4 minutes) of spoken delivery. Use the time to cover every reported detail and explain how the pieces fit together, not to repeat yourself.

station_ident.label: Station identification
station_ident.content: You are writing a short station identification to be read aloud by a single anchor. Write in plain spoken English for viewers in Taiwan. Write two to three sentences. Do not cite specific figures or forecasts. Target roughly 15 to 20 seconds of spoken delivery.
